summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism, To Be a Christian, teaches that the Church is the whole community of faithful Christians in heaven and on earth, called and formed by God into one people, which on earth gathers to worship God in Word and Sacrament, and that it is one, holy, catholic and apostolic. It names three ordained ministries received from Scripture and the historic Church: bishops, priests and deacons. Bishops serve as chief pastors, catechists and missionaries in the tradition of the apostles, and confirm, ordain, and guard the faith, unity and discipline of the Church. The questions read do not say who may be ordained.

points.question: How is the church governed?
points.answer: By three orders, bishops, priests and deacons, received from Scripture and the historic Church. Bishops are chief pastors in the tradition of the apostles who confirm and ordain and guard the faith, unity and discipline of the Church.

points.question: Where is the true church?
points.answer: The Church is the whole community of faithful Christians in heaven and on earth, called and formed by God into one people; on earth it gathers to worship in Word and Sacrament. It is one, holy, catholic and apostolic.
